verdict: OK to lend in Chennai auto OEM/dealer chain, but only to borrowers with real cash conversion — the local GST signal (-3.2% Apr-to-date) [D] means we lend selectively, not broadly.
title: Chennai cars & commercial vehicles (OEM): a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
**A car or CV OEM turns steel, castings, electronics and labour into vehicles, and the cash comes back through dealers and fleet buyers, not from the factory gate.** The OEM holds the brand and the pricing power; the dealer holds inventory and the receivable; the fleet operator holds the vehicle and earns per kilometre. **Value sits with whoever controls the model and the service network; cash sits one step down the chain, in the dealer's floorplan and the fleet's monthly billing.** So when a proposal lands, first fix which of these three the borrower actually is, because the working-capital cycle and the collateral are completely different.

## Where the cash and the risk sit now
**National output is running hot: IIP for NIC 29 is +25.2% YoY and +19.2% Apr-to-date [D].** Peer results confirm the volume side — Tata Motors CV volumes rose 26% with net profit of Rs 2,560 crore, though commodity inflation forced price increases [6]; M&M's automotive revenue grew 25% to ₹31,115 crore with EBIT margin at 9.5% [5]. **The margin line is the soft spot: analysts expect Q4FY26 EBITDA growth of about 21% but flag commodity pressure [4], and rising raw material and freight costs are expected to weigh on margins [7].** Note [4] and [7] are peer commentary from April and July 2026, so treat them as dated.

**The local picture is weaker than the national one: Tamil Nadu GST collections are -3.2% Apr-to-date against India +6.1%, a 9.3 pp gap [D].** That is a demand signal in this state, and it sits alongside bank credit growing +27.0% YoY against output +19.2%, a +7.8 pp gap [D] — money is moving into the sector faster than vehicles are being made. **So when a proposal lands, check whether the borrower's own sales are growing with the national number or shrinking with the state GST; if the latter, ask what changed in their order book.**

## Where the growth is in Chennai
**The live opportunity here is electric last-mile cargo, and it is small and new.** Montra Electric and Chennai-based VFRYT flagged off 50 Super Cargo eCX d+ units (13.8 kWh battery, over 150 km range, 170 cubic feet cargo) inside an inaugural fleet of about 185 electric vehicles [2][3]. **Pursue the owner-driver and small fleet operator buying into this platform, and the dealers and service shops that support them — not the platform itself on unsecured terms.** The local sources say nothing about Chennai's overall OEM volumes or dealer margins, so lean on the national IIP and peer numbers above and collect from customer anything city-specific.

## How to grow safely
**Structure against the asset and the cash flow, not the brand.** For a fleet buyer, take hypothecation of the vehicle, a monthly repayment sized to per-kilometre earnings, and a personal guarantee from the owner-driver. **Every month take the vehicle's running log or FASTag trip data, the platform payout statement, and the EMI bounce record** — the platform tracks GPS, SIM and FASTag [1][3], so the data exists. For a dealer, take stock statements and the OEM's confirmed order book. **Avoid borrowers whose only collateral is a purchase order from a new platform, and avoid anyone funding inventory with the +7.8 pp credit-output gap [D] as their growth story.**

## Early-warning signs
**Watch the state GST number monthly: if Tamil Nadu stays negative while India stays positive [D], tighten new fleet exposures.** Watch commodity-driven price hikes [6] — if the borrower cannot pass them on, margin goes first. Watch platform concentration: a fleet whose entire book rides on one marketplace [1][2] has one counterparty. Watch EMI bounces and trip-data gaps together; a vehicle that stops moving stops earning.
watch: two more negative prints vs India positive [D] -> stop new fleet lending in Chennai
utilisation falls below the level assumed at sanction -> reprice or recall
first bounce -> site visit and restructure before second
hike not passed to buyer [6] -> cut dealer inventory limits
VFRYT or Montra changes terms [1][2] -> review all fleet exposures tied to it
